text: UI Scripts, stored in the sys_ui_script table, are reusable client-side JavaScript libraries. A UI Script isn't tied to any single form, any single Client Script, or any single UI Page — it's a standalone record you write once and call from anywhere in the instance that needs it, which is exactly the problem that solves copy-pasting the same helper function into five different places.

Here's a UI Script named DateFormatHelpers, holding one plain function called formatShortDate. It checks whether the incoming date string is empty and returns an empty string if so, otherwise it builds a Date object and assembles a short month, day, and year string from it. Notice nothing in this script is attached to any table, any form, or any specific record type — it's pure, portable JavaScript.

A Client Script can then include that UI Script by name and call formatShortDate directly. Here, inside an onLoad function, it reads the record's created-on value and formats it into an info message shown to the user. Because the UI Script isn't marked Global, it only loads on the pages that explicitly include it, rather than loading on every single page in the instance whether that page needs it or not.

The real parallel is Chapter 3's Script Includes. A Script Include shares server-side logic across Business Rules and other server scripts, so you write a function once instead of five times. A UI Script does the exact same thing, just for client-side logic shared across Client Scripts and UI Pages. The mechanics differ — no classes, no GlideAjax boundary, just plain functions loaded straight into the page — but the underlying motivation is identical: one place to fix a bug or extend behavior instead of several.

Reach for a UI Script the moment the same client-side function shows up a second time, in a second Client Script or a second UI Page. One copy is fine to leave inline. A second copy is the signal to extract it into a shared UI Script and have both callers include it, applying the exact same discipline Chapter 3 taught for server code to the browser side of the application. Next up: the Advanced UI Lab, combining a GlideModal confirmation with a shared UI Script in one real build.
